DERIVATION is core model s3 pattern 1: data/spain_2012_reality.do reads DA2973 by infix with the CIS variable names lowercased ('p34 134 p35 135', copied from ES2973's DATA LIST 'P34 134 P35 135') and Bookmark 8 loops gen item = the literal names, so the IRW item code IS the CIS variable name; nothing positional, Step 5b exempt, no verification_/verify_ files written. COLUMN CROSS-CHECK: three level-1 records agree for both items -- ES2973 DATA LIST positions 134/135, ES2973 VARIABLE LABELS (/P34 'Frecuencia con la que habla de política', /P35 'Frecuencia con la que se hablaba de política en casa durante la infancia/adolescencia'), and the printed questionnaire's column markers (134) under P.34 and (135) under P.35; the labels' now vs childhood content cannot be swapped without being self-evident (asserted in .cache/spain_2012_reality_conversation/build.R). TEXT (text_source=study_materials): item_text = the printed P.34/P.35 question wording. The questionnaire PDFs are scanned images with no text layer (pdftotext returns nothing, no OCR installed), so the wording was read visually from a 200-dpi render of page 5 and typed; spot-check character by character is advisable. Versions A and B print P.34/P.35 identically (FT2973 footnote: the versions differ only in P.9, 12, 15, 21, 24, 26 and 29), so pooling A and B respondents in one table is correct. Dropped: the 'P.34'/'P.35' numbering and the interviewer direction '(MOSTRAR TARJETA Q).' (sibling precedent, batch_512 acceptability / batch_515 punishment); line wraps joined. Two stand-alone questions with their own stems -> each full question in item_text, instructions and section_prompt blank, one trivial section_id. Both asked of all respondents (no filter printed). OPTIONS: ES2973 VALUE LABELS identical on P34 and P35 (asserted): 1 'Con mucha frecuencia' 2 'De vez en cuando' 3 'Pocas veces' 4 'Prácticamente nunca' 8 'No recuerda' 9 'N.C.'; the printed questionnaire lists the same labels over codes 1 2 3 4 8 9. option_text ships the four substantive labels for resp 1-4 on both items; both items use all four levels. SENTINELS: the .do sets 8/9 to missing and drops those rows. Dropped from raw DA2973 (8/9): p34 10/4, p35 124/5 (143 total; 5924-143 = 5781). REBUILD, decisive for plumbing: DA2973 (2962 records, all width 392, ESTUDIO=2973 on every record, id = row number) cols 134-135 minus 8/9, cov_sex col 160 (P42), cov_age cols 384-385 (99 -> missing) reproduces the live table exactly: 5781 rows both, 2955 ids both, 0 only-live / 0 only-rebuilt id-item keys, 0 duplicate id-item keys, 0 resp / 0 cov_age mismatches, cov_sex Hombre 2871 / Mujer 2910 all on the diagonal (.cache/spain_2012_reality_conversation/rebuild.R; live read from the local irw cache populated by table_context.R). Live item x resp (1..4): p34 627/791/792/738, p35 308/539/781/1205 (identical to raw DA2973). Coherent: childhood household talk skews to 'prácticamente nunca' (1205); r(p34,p35)=0.41. STEP 3b: dictionary Description ('Frequency of political conversation now and in childhood') and the .do header 'conversation (P34, P35), 1-4 frequency of talking about politics now and at home during childhood' describe P.34/P.35; 2 items, resp 1..4 match; no mismatch. validate_items.R --table-sets PASS (2 items, resp 1..4). language=Spanish; translation_source=machine_translation (CIS publishes Estudio 2973 in Spanish only; the _translated columns are English written by IRW; issues-page line owed once live). public_note: Codes run 1 = Con mucha frecuencia (very often) to 4 = Prácticamente nunca (practically never), so higher means less political talk; 'No recuerda' and no-answer are stored as missing; item text English is IRW machine translation of the Spanish-only CIS questionnaire
